notes.fact: Kyiv Independent reports a hours-long Russian missile and drone attack overnight killed at least three people in Kyiv and damaged three Dnipro bridges. Power, heating and water were disrupted.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Kyiv, Nov 20

notes.fact: AP says local authorities report three dead and nine injured in Kyiv. Mayor Klitschko says Podilskyi bridge was closed to traffic and the Darnytskyi bridge was also damaged.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Kyiv, Nov 20

notes.fact: The National (UAE) reports at least five dead across Kyiv and Lviv overnight, with Russia's defence ministry saying it hit port infrastructure in Odesa region and downed 310 Ukrainian drones.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Kyiv, Nov 20

notes.fact: Kyiv Post says ballistic missiles damaged the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges. The Southern bridge stayed partly open, with weight limits for vehicles.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Kyiv, Nov 20

notes.fact: South Korea's SBS, citing Reuters and AFP, says the Kyiv strikes came right after the Shenzhen summit. Kyiv has only eight bridges linking its two banks.
notes.event: Russian mass strike on Kyiv, Nov 20

notes.fact: Bloomberg reports projectiles from a Russian airstrike damaged the Dutch and Austrian embassies in central Kyiv on Thursday afternoon. Both governments reported no injuries.
Reuters-sourced reports say Putin, in Shenzhen, vowed a response 'far more painful' than the bridge damage. He said he was dropping any moratorium on energy and sea attacks.
notes.event: Crimean Bridge strikes and Putin response

notes.fact: LBC reports Putin said he had asked his Security Council to consider a sea and energy attack moratorium. After the bridge strikes, he said there would be no agreements.
notes.event: Crimean Bridge strikes and Putin response

notes.fact: A Moscow Times and TASS-sourced summary says Putin called the bridge civilian. He said talks on Ukraine could continue with no deadlines and that he sees no insurmountable obstacles.
notes.event: Crimean Bridge strikes and Putin response

notes.fact: ABC/AP says Ukraine's General Staff confirmed Neptune missile strikes on rail tracks Wednesday night. Russia's Transport Ministry said rail traffic was suspended with no casualties.
notes.event: Crimean Bridge strikes and Putin response
notes.claim_by: party:Ukraine's General Staff; Russia's Transport Ministry

notes.fact: WSJ reports Kushner floated NATO membership for Ukraine if it cedes territory. Sources say it came up at a Dublin meeting; Moscow's paper demands the opposite.
notes.event: US NATO-for-Donbas idea and Berlin meeting

notes.fact: Investing coverage of the WSJ story says Zelensky confirmed the question was raised and repeated that Ukraine will not give up land. A US official says many ideas are under discussion.
notes.event: US NATO-for-Donbas idea and Berlin meeting

notes.fact: Time reports European leaders at a Berlin Coalition of the Willing meeting pledged support for Ukraine 'as long as it takes'. Merz said a Yalta-style format will not bring peace.
notes.event: US NATO-for-Donbas idea and Berlin meeting

notes.fact: A summary says Trump told the Berlin gathering Putin wants to end the war. Estonia's and Poland's leaders called European reaction sceptical or very cautious, with Tusk doubting serious talks before winter.
notes.event: US NATO-for-Donbas idea and Berlin meeting

notes.fact: CBS reports the Senate rejected H.Con.Res. 93 by 48-51, with Collins, Murkowski and Paul voting in favour. It was the first vote since the Nov. 3 midterms.
The Hill reports Pentagon official Arthur Miller said the Iran war has cost $48.3 billion as of Nov. 13, up from just over $47 billion in October. Damage to US bases is excluded.
IANS, citing Xinhua and the NYT, says Congress has held 21 Iran war powers votes since February. A June Senate measure was the only one to clear both chambers.
Foreign Policy says the US and Iran resumed strikes over the past week, ending a roughly two-month lull. Iran hit US assets in Bahrain and an air base in Kuwait.
Trump told Axios he is 'not rushing' a decision on Iran and will wait until after the new year. Israel's Times of Israel carried the quote.

Axios, via Israel National News, says Netanyahu is pressing for a four-to-seven-day joint strike. Options reportedly include Pickaxe Mountain; Gulf leaders and advisers urge more time for economic pressure.
Axios, via Times of Israel, says the White House asked the Pentagon and intelligence agencies whether Iran could be struck without triggering attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure.
TradingView, relaying UKMTO, says a vessel off Oman was hit by an unknown projectile while transiting Hormuz on Thursday. An analyst says the US naval blockade of Iran continues.
Iran International reports Iranian leader's adviser Mokhber said the Shenzhen summit showed the US can no longer rally countries against Iran. He called Hormuz security a red line.
Breitbart says Qatari mediators met Iran's foreign minister in Oman this week without a breakthrough. Tehran demands an end to the blockade; Washington demands nuclear concessions.
Al Jazeera says Saudi civil defence reported a Houthi attack damaged a tower in Riyadh's financial district, with no injuries. Images from state media identified it as the PIF tower.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Riyadh PIF tower

notes.fact: Reuters, via SOFX, cites three sources saying a Houthi missile hit the tower directly, while the coalition cited falling debris. AFP witnesses described windows blown out across several floors.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Riyadh PIF tower

notes.fact: The National reports Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said cruise missiles targeted Riyadh's airport and financial centre in response to Saudi attacks on Yemen. Saba reported Saudi air strikes on Sanaa.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Riyadh PIF tower

notes.fact: The New Arab says Qatar, Kuwait and the GCC condemned the attack. It says it occurred ahead of US CENTCOM chief Brad Cooper's meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman.
notes.event: Houthi strike on Riyadh PIF tower

notes.fact: AFRICOM says it struck al-Shabaab on Nov. 17 near Yaaq Shiniile, about 40 km northwest of Kismayo, in coordination with Somalia's government. It gave no casualty information.
Antiwar.com says AFRICOM reported at least five strikes between Nov. 13-15, mostly near Leego, putting its 2026 count at 97. It says New America's tally, including media-reported strikes, is 103.

Antiwar.com, citing a Drop Site journalist, says Somali security officials report at least eight US-trained Danab troops killed in an al-Shabaab ambush on Nov. 12. Single-source; not independently confirmed.
FTL Somalia reports AFRICOM described its Nov. 17 strikes as aimed at degrading al-Shabaab's ability to threaten US forces and citizens. It says the command withholds damage assessments.
Reuters via Al Jazeera: the ICJ ruled Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017, the first time it has held a state responsible. Compensation terms come later.
AFP, via Yahoo, says Myanmar's presidential spokeswoman called the ruling 'not fair' because it was not unanimous. China raised concerns of judicial overreach; the US urged avoiding politicisation.
Fox News says officials found no evidence that a 10-day wave of outages hit Microsoft, banks, airlines and agencies through a coordinated cyberattack. FBI says it will keep monitoring.
notes.event: US outage wave and cyber attribution

notes.fact: DNI Jay Clayton said he sees no sign of a coordinated cyberattack or state activity, blaming security patching and upgrades. Fox links this to Reuters reports of an attack on about 200 websites.
notes.event: US outage wave and cyber attribution

notes.fact: ABC7 reports JPMorgan Chase said third-party service providers were hit by a cyberattack. It said attackers accessed marketing data that may include customer names and email addresses.
CISA urged immediate patching of Oracle Java flaw CVE-2026-114938 ('Java4Shell'), which can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Java is widely used in US systems.
CISA's advisory list shows a Nov. 5 joint fact sheet from US government partners urging hardening of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems.
WaterISAC's bulletin lists a members-only situation report, updated Nov. 12, on heightened risk of Iranian cyber retaliation following US strikes on Iran. Contents are not public.
Konbriefing's tracker lists 2026 attacks on US water utilities: Minnesota towns in July, New Jersey in August with a suspected Iran link, and a Michigan well. Service continued in each case.
Konbriefing lists a Nov. 9 cyber incident at Ridgecrest Regional Hospital in California that disrupted phones and computers, and an Oct. 26 attack on the University of New Mexico health system.
